neighbours.label: A phrase that points back to things already named ('a combination of the two', 'a pot of the same name', 'dependent on it'), firing on 'two', 'name' or 'it'; the same sentences with the referent spelled out stay quiet.
fire: You can pay by card or in cash, or use a mix of the two.
The soup is served in a bowl of the same name.
Farmers grow rice and beans, and many grow both of the two.
The town gave its name to the cheese of the same name.
Tea or coffee? I could never choose between the two.
The lake lies beside a village of the same name.
Some prefer the train, some the bus; I use neither of the two.
The dance comes from the region of the same name.
quiet: You can pay by card or in cash at the front desk.
The soup is served in a deep bowl with bread.
Farmers grow rice and beans on the river plain.
The town is famous for its soft cheese.
Tea or coffee? I usually drink tea in the morning.
The lake lies beside a small fishing village.
Some prefer the train, some the bus, some the car.
The dance comes from the mountains in the north.

short: pointing back to named things ('the two', 'same name')
notes: Card: no single token (' two' x3, ' below' x3, ' it' x3, ' known' x3: a combination of the two; see below; a clay pot of the same name; dependent on it). Exploratory probe: 'of the two' 0.43, 'of the same name' 0.35, 'on it' 0.17, 'see below' 0.14; same sentences without the back-reference 0.006-0.015. The test keeps to 'the two' and 'the same name'.
